[Doc][Misc] Document Ascend Docker Runtime container setup (#21712)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Every model tutorial's **4.1 Docker Image Installation** section spells
out each NPU device node (`--device /dev/davinci0` … up to 16 lines on
A3) and the driver mounts (`/usr/local/dcmi`, `/usr/local/bin/npu-smi`,
`/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64`). The same block is repeated in 27
pages, and the only differences between A2, A3, and 950DT Products are
the image tag, the number of DIE devices, and a few host files.

This PR makes Ascend Docker Runtime the container form used by the
tutorials and documents it in the installation guide.

**Installation guide (`getting_started/installation.md`)**

- The install and verification steps now live in **Set up the software
environment > Use Ascend Docker Runtime**, above the three installation
paths, because both container paths (prebuilt image and CANN
environment) need it on the host.
- Install and verify: `chmod u+x`, `.run --install` as root, `systemctl
daemon-reload && systemctl restart docker`, and a `docker info --format`
check for `default=ascend`, including the `--runtime ascend` and
`daemon.json` fallbacks when it prints `runc`.
- Custom mounts through `ASCEND_RUNTIME_MOUNTS`: the value **replaces**
the default set, so `base` has to be listed explicitly
(`base,hostextra`); `base.list` is no longer edited by hand.
- **Additional guides > Manual device mapping without Ascend Docker
Runtime**: the explicit device and driver flags for Atlas A2, Atlas A3,
950DT products, Atlas 300I DUO, and Atlas 200I Pro, for hosts that
choose not to install the runtime. The runtime instructions, the shared
fragment, and the Quick Start page link to it.

**Tutorials (27 pages)**

- Each container section now opens with one shared note: it says the
commands need Ascend Docker Runtime on the host, what the runtime
mounts, that the guide assumes 26.3.0 or later, and where the manual
device mapping fallback is. The note lives in one fragment,
`getting_started/installation/ascend_docker_runtime.inc.md`, included by
the 27 tutorial pages, so it cannot drift apart.
- Each "Docker Image Installation" section drops the device and driver
flags and selects the NPUs with `ASCEND_VISIBLE_DEVICES` (A2 `0-7`, A3
`0-15`, 950DT `0-7`, Atlas 300I DUO `0-7` or `0`, Atlas 200I Pro `0`),
keeping the product-specific mounts, weight and cache directories, and
container options.
- The values keep the device counts of the removed `--device` lines, so
a page that used one NPU still selects one ID.
- Later chapters that start a second container with SSD or MemCache
devices keep their explicit flags; they do not set
`ASCEND_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, so they work with or without the runtime
installed.

Net diff: 55 files, +454 / -1777; the 27 tutorial pages drop 1,375
lines, almost all of them per-device lines and driver mounts.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Documentation only, so no release note fragment is required.

### How was this patch tested?

- `mkdocs build --strict` on this branch: builds cleanly, the new
section and all 27 tutorial pages render (including tabbed code blocks),
and the tutorial links resolve to
`installation.html#installation-ascend-docker-runtime`.
- Behavior claims checked against the Ascend-docker-runtime 26.1.0 run
package:
- `run_main.sh`: the installer requires root, accepts
`--install-scene=docker|containerd|isula` (`crio` only in newer
releases), and writes `/etc/ascend-docker-runtime.d/base.list`.
- `base.list`: `/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64`,
`/usr/local/Ascend/driver/include`, `/usr/local/dcmi`,
`/usr/local/bin/npu-smi`, `/var/queue_schedule`.
- `hook/process/process.go`: `parseMounts` returns `["base"]` for an
empty value or one longer than 128 characters and lowercases the
comma-separated names; `readMountConfig` skips paths that do not exist
and rejects a file above 128 entries.
- Default mount lists per product, and the UB devices and tools, checked
against the MindCluster container documentation.
- Built site check: all 27 tutorial pages contain the shared note and
link to `installation.html#installation-ascend-docker-runtime`;
markdownlint and codespell pass on the changed files.
- The basic container start (only `ASCEND_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, no
`--device` or driver `-v` flags) was validated earlier on an A3 host
with runtime 26.1.0 and remains the basis of the first commit.
- The tutorial commands were transformed from the existing
explicit-`--device` blocks with the same device counts; they were not
re-executed on every product. The Quick Start path, which the doctest
workflow covers, gained the runtime requirement and the verification
paragraph; its hardware commands only dropped the device and driver
flags.

[Feature][KV Pool] Enable prefill KV offload for GLM-5.3 (#22742)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable GLM-5.3 prefill KV offload with BF16 and FP8 C8. For single-group
offload, reshape the shared slot to match the component layout with
offload disabled so P/D can use the same transfer layout.

```text
FP8 C8 Indexer
  Offload disabled  [K0][K1] [scale0][scale1]  (native buffer)
  Offload enabled   [K0][K1] [scale0][scale1]  (shared slot)

BF16 main MLA
  Offload disabled  [NoPE0][NoPE1]              (NoPE tensor)
                    [RoPE0][RoPE1]              (RoPE tensor)
  Offload enabled   [NoPE0][NoPE1] [RoPE0][RoPE1]  (shared slot)
```

Mooncake Push with offload depends on #21891.

#### P/D startup

Use the V2 runner on separate P and D hosts with matching KV cache
formats and a shared MemCache service. The P example uses four shared
buffers per block-stride bucket.

**P node**

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" --kv-transfer-config '{
  "kv_connector": "MultiConnector",
  "kv_role": "kv_producer",
  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
    "connectors": [
      {"kv_connector": "MooncakePushConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer"},
      {
        "kv_connector": "AscendStoreConnector",
        "kv_role": "kv_producer",
        "kv_connector_extra_config": {
          "backend": "memcache",
          "use_layerwise": true,
          "layerwise_num_shared_buffers": 4,
          "layerwise_independent_layers": []
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}'
```

**D node**

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" --kv-transfer-config '{
  "kv_connector": "MultiConnector",
  "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
    "connectors": [
      {"kv_connector": "MooncakePushConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer"},
      {
        "kv_connector": "AscendStoreConnector",
        "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
        "kv_connector_extra_config": {
          "backend": "memcache",
          "use_layerwise": false
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}'
```

[Feature] QLI v2: candidate-driven execution, QSLI metadata operator, and arch22 performance optimizations (#21394)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds candidate-driven execution to the Quant Lightning Indexer
(QLI) v2
kernel on arch22, introduces a standalone QSLI (quant sparse lightning
indexer)
metadata operator, and lands a series of verified performance
optimizations and
correctness fixes for Ascend 910B-class hardware.

**Why:** QLI v2 scoring is dominated by scanning the full KV sequence,
while in
decode and long-context workloads most blocks cannot reach the top-K
anyway. The
candidate-driven design lets the producer emit a compact candidate block
list and
its length, so the consumer can restrict its work to those candidates
instead of
scanning everything. Previously this path existed in the kernel but was
not
reachable from production: the mode=2 entry ignored
`candidate_block_length`, and
the source path (mode=1) did not produce it.

**What it does:**

1. **Kernel optimizations (arch22)** — adaptive Top-K accumulator width
and
Level-0 vector-repeat dispatch (from #20303); query/weight resident in
L0A;
   block-level hit-bitmap candidate mask; fully vectorized block-level
   mask/kscale/index generation; candidate tile 256→512 tokens;
ping-pong score/kscale prefetch; threshold pruning with row-level early
exit;
   hardware compare + `Select` mask chain.
2. **Candidate-driven pipeline** — `candidate_mode=2` with
`candidate_block_length`: staging gather / cube QK / vector scoring
TopK,
8-slot semaphore ring, W double buffering, score double buffering, and a
   pending queue for deferred cross-task consumption.
3. **QSLI metadata operator** — new AICPU operator
`VllmAscendQuantSparseLightningIndexerMetadata` that schedules work by
`max(L)×8` tokens with candidate tiles, plus QSLI candidate × FD/LD
fusion.
4. **Cross-core reduction (LD) on 910B** — LD was previously
Ascend950-only; it
is now enabled on 910B, and block-level topk spill/reduce was added so
mode=1
   block outputs also work under LD.
5. **Closed source→consumer loop** — mode=1 now optionally emits
`candidate_block_length` (DSL semantics: candidate blocks of 8 tokens),
and
the adapter consumer passes it through and builds QSLI metadata on
demand.
6. **Correctness fixes** found during validation: LD slot addressing and
`DataCopyExtParams.srcStride` units; NaN poisoning from stale invalid
slots;
   FD last-tile non-integral-block precision (L=321 class); score-region
ping-pong overwritten by a third task on the same core; aux(kscale)
region
parity overwrite (period 2→4); and a cube K-load handshake lost during
the
   upstream merge.

This is a large PR (22 commits, 46 files). Each commit message contains
the
detailed design notes, measurements, and validation evidence for that
step;
reviewing commit by commit is recommended.

**Measured results** (msprof device-side Task Duration on Ascend 910B3
unless
noted; same-environment paired controls):

| Change | Workload | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q/W resident in L0A | cases A / B | −6.9% / −5.7% |
| Block-level hit bitmap | case C candidate consumer | −16.9% |
| Vectorized candidate consumption | case C, L=2048 | 2491.8 → 675.4 µs
(−72.9%) |
| Candidate tile 256→512 | case C, L=2048 | 690.9 → 544.5 µs (−21.2%) |
| Threshold pruning | case C | 525.9 → 485.0 µs (−7.8%) |
| Row-level early exit | case C | 479.8 → ~323 µs (~−33%) |
| QSLI candidate × FD fusion | decode B16/S1=1/S2=128K | 137.4 → 125.1
µs (−9.0%) |
| Block-level LD for mode=1 | cand1_src | 0.181 → 0.145 ms (−19.9%) |

The row-level early-exit number was measured with torch aclprof
(calibrated
against msprof Task Duration within 0.06%) and was still pending an
msprof
re-check.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, but additively only:

- `npu_quant_lightning_indexer_v3` gains an optional input
`candidate_block_length` and an optional output
`candidate_block_length_out`
  (`int32`, `[rows, N2]`, allocated only in source mode).
- New AICPU operator `VllmAscendQuantSparseLightningIndexerMetadata` for
QSLI
  metadata.
- Existing call sites and modes keep their current behavior (the old
2-output
entry receives an empty placeholder); outputs are row-by-row identical
to the
  previous implementation on all regression cases.
- The adapter-internal `_qli_newapi_block_length` helper is removed
because the
  kernel now produces the length; no other public Python API changes.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Vendor e2e regression:** 17 cases (mode=1 / mode=3 /
candidate-source / FD /
  mask0 / topk2048 / prefill / g64), row-by-row identical to pre-change
  baselines (dump A/B), including block-level outputs.
- **Generalization sweep:** 33/33 cases — unaligned L, multi-batch,
varlen,

- **Boundary coverage:** `L ∈ {1, 63, 64, 65, 321, 2047, 2048}`; L=321
×10;
`L ∈ {321, 325, 352, 383, 384, 385, 449, 511, 512, 2048}`; empty rows
and

metadata
  ABI, `QLI_CHECK_QSLI_META=1` self-check.
- **New e2e test:** `test_quant_lightning_indexer_vector_repeats.py` for
the
  Level-0 vector-repeat dispatch.
- **Performance:** msprof device-side Task Duration (30/23/26-run
protocols as
noted per commit), with same-session interleaved A/B controls for small
deltas.

[Feature][A3] Support W4A8 MegaMoe shared-expert fusion (#22128)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Builds on #22207 to enable MegaMoE shared-expert fusion on A3 for
DeepSeek V4.1 with W4A8 (INT4) routed experts and a dynamic W8A8 (INT8)
shared expert.

- Passes shared weights and scales through both W4A8 weight storage
paths to MegaMoE, reusing the shared INT8 descriptors from #22207.
- Loads full shared weights on each TP rank when shared-expert DP is
enabled for the A3 main model.
- Checks for a CANN interface with independent routed and shared weight
descriptors. The runner skips the separate shared MLP only when the
shared weights are ready and the current forward uses MegaMoE.
- Sizes the A3 mode-3 symmetric buffer for the profiling token budget on
decode-only nodes, including the 432-request, 512-profile-token case.

### Does this PR introduce *any* user-facing change?

Yes. On A3, a supported W4A8 model can now fuse its dynamic W8A8 shared
expert with the routed experts. With a matching CANN operator package,
keep `--enable-expert-parallel` and add the following fields to the
existing `--additional-config` JSON.

```json
{"enable_fused_mc2": 3, "enable_shared_expert_dp": true}
```

### How was this patch tested?

- Ruff lint, Ruff format, Python syntax parsing and `git diff --check`
passed on the updated source.
- Statically checked that the A3 CANN 9.3 B106 Python wheel exposes the
shared weights, scales and dtype arguments required by the mixed
INT4/INT8 path. Also verified PD service startup and real-model
inference on the r140 A3 image with the matching prebuilt B106 operator
package. The r140 measurements are reported below.
- Updated regression coverage for ABI detection, W4A8 payload
forwarding, shared weight replication, runner fallback and decode-only
profiling capacity.

**A3 r140 validation (2026-11-23 to 2026-11-24)**

Tested revision `df8eceedaac2e9836043863236e73b8bc8ca10aa` on two Ascend
A3 nodes using the ARM64 main r140 image (CANN 9.3.0), the matching B106
MegaMoE operator package, and `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w4a8` weights.
The image pinned vLLM at `4ba787ec` and vLLM-Ascend at `c12397a0`. The
performance baseline is r140 + #22207. The candidate adds #22128. Both
use the same weights, package, service flags and workload, with no
additional code patches.

**Pure decode performance**

Both variants use P DP4/TP1/PCP4, D DP16/TP1/PCP1, `enable_fused_mc2=3`
on P and D, P-side EPLB, MooncakeConnectorV2, fixed DSpark5, V2 Model
Runner, FASTOKENS and four proxy workers. D uses
`max_num_batched_tokens=432`, `max_num_seqs=72` and
`gpu_memory_utilization=0.95`. Startup evidence confirms that the
baseline executes the shared expert separately for A3 W4A8 and the
candidate takes the fused path.

Each case used the same 128K input and 1,024-token output, one fully
warmed P-side prefix, and request rate 0 (unpaced). Throughput is
steady-state D-side generated tokens/s. The baseline averages two
repetitions. For each candidate case, the highest and lowest throughput
of six repetitions were dropped, and latency metrics use the same four
retained runs.

| Concurrency / requests | Steady D throughput, tok/s | Mean TTFT, s |
Mean TPOT, ms | Mean ITL, ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 306 / 1,224 | 9,910.08 → 11,230.84 (**+13.33%**) | 1.741 → 1.605
(−7.82%) | 28.90 → 25.03 (−13.41%) | 109.45 → 95.33 (−12.91%) |
| 432 / 1,728 | 11,123.47 → 11,441.82 (+2.86%) | 6.714 → 8.844 (+31.72%)
| 31.60 → 28.15 (−10.92%) | 119.25 → 106.18 (−10.96%) |

At 306 concurrency, the candidate is also 5.37% above the faster
baseline run. At 432 concurrency, the throughput difference is within
observed run-to-run variation. Decode capacity queueing increased, and
TTFT rose even as TPOT and ITL improved. Neither variant recorded D-side
preemptions or recompute warnings during these runs.

**Accuracy with #22128**

The scores below are from candidate runs. No matching r140 run without
#22128 was evaluated for either dataset, so these scores cannot
establish an accuracy delta attributable to the PR.

| Benchmark | Result |
|---|---|
| GPQA Diamond (AISBench, dataset revision `b1ed2c`) | **178 / 198
correct (89.90%)**, with **100%** answer extraction. Native AISBench
score. |
| DeepSWE | **85 passed, 27 failed, 1 unjudged** out of 113 tasks.
**75.22%** confirmed passes over all tasks, **75.89%** over the 112
judged tasks. A verifier timeout on both the original attempt and the
single retry left the full-suite score incomplete. |

Verified on Ascend 910B (vLLM 0.33.0, CANN 9.3.0): visible=2,3 with

[Performance][Model] Reuse DeepSeek V4.1 routing input IDs across DP/PCP (#19679)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4.1 hash and vision routers need token IDs in the same row
order as the router logits. On the `ALLGATHER` path, successive MoE
layers repeat the same collective within a decoder segment.

The first eligible layer gathers the IDs after its MoE prepare step has
established the SP/DP/PCP row layout. It copies the result into
model-owned storage at a fixed address. Later layers read the active
rows. The cache preserves the input dtype (INT32 or INT64) and the raw
`-1` sentinel. The fused Hash TopK operator handles the sentinel on
load. The PyTorch vision path normalizes its own input before indexing.

The decoder prefix and bounded-replay tail each have a producer and
separate storage because replay can compact rows. Each producer
refreshes its buffer on every execution of its segment. Model
initialization uses the communication policy at the largest supported
padded batch to skip allocation where `ALLGATHER` is unreachable. Other
communication paths and concurrent microbatches prepare IDs per layer.

[Performance][KV Transfer] Support per-request Mooncake V2 pulls (#20903)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Mooncake V2 currently waits for every READ in a producer-engine batch
before reporting request completion. A request whose KV is ready can
therefore wait for unrelated transfers before decode becomes runnable.

This PR defaults to submitting and completing requests independently.
Each request retains its batch index for replica selection and reuses
block mappings across layers and PP ranks. Future callbacks report
completion only after all submitted READs for that request finish,
including after a partial submission failure. Later requests can
complete independently.

The receive loop selects its batch or per-request queue processor once
at initialization. Each processor owns queue completion and exception
handling. Callback-registration failures drain submitted READs through
an idempotent completion path; unexpected batch-aggregation failures
drain known READs before reporting failure. Unexpected bookkeeping
failures are logged so other producer engines can continue; requests
whose completion cannot be established are retained rather than
releasing potentially in-flight blocks.

Both modes prepare addresses and execute synchronous READs in the
transfer pool. Batch mode retains aggregated READs and its completion
barrier. Thread-pool configuration is shared in the base worker and also
applies to Push sending workers. Block-hash handling and NumPy address
optimizations are outside this PR.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Configure these options in `kv_connector_extra_config`:

| Option | Default | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pull_transfer_mode` | `"request"` | Pull only, on D: independent
request submission/completion. Use `"batch"` for aggregated READs and
batch completion. |
| `transfer_max_workers` | `32` | Positive integer controlling the
transfer pool per worker: D-side READs for Pull, P-side sends for Push.
Booleans and strings are rejected. |

```json
{"kv_connector_extra_config": {"pull_transfer_mode": "request", "transfer_max_workers": 32}}
```

For Push, set only `transfer_max_workers` on P. The peer requires no
matching setting. This replaces the earlier draft's `pull_max_workers`
option. Request mode can increase READ call overhead; its end-to-end
performance benefit has not been established.

### How was this patch tested?

- Focused tests cover shared pool configuration, Push pool wiring, READ
granularity and byte-range equivalence, independent completion after
submission/READ failures, callback registration failures before/after
attachment, immediate/repeated callbacks, and continued processing of
another producer engine after an unexpected handler or batch-aggregation
failure.
- **26 local CPU source-isolated cases passed** using actual production
methods and test functions, synthetic metadata, real Futures/threads and
mocked device/transport initialization. These are not full torch/vLLM
runtime pytest results.
- `format.sh ci` passed for enabled hooks, including Ruff, codespell,

commits.message:
[BugFix][Quantization] Pad odd W4A8-MXFP4 MoE down_proj scale groups under TP (#21399)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`AscendW4A8MXFPDynamicFusedMoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading`
reshapes `w2_weight_scale`'s
last dimension into pairs of MX groups. A TP shard can leave
`intermediate_size_per_partition // group_size` odd (e.g.
`moe_intermediate_size=2304`,
`group_size=32`, `tensor_parallel_size=8` gives `288 // 32 = 9`), which
crashes the reshape
with a shape mismatch.

This is the same class of bug as #20398 / #20573 (DS-original W8A8 MXFP8
linear path hitting
an odd scale-group count under TP), just in the FP4 MoE routed-expert
path. Pads with one
zero group before reshaping, mirroring that fix and vLLM upstream's own
MXFP4 scale-alignment
pad (`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/mxfp4_utils.py`).

**Caveat (updated):** unlike the W8A8 MXFP8 fix, this only pads
`w2_weight_scale`, not
`w2_weight` itself. I looked for a kernel-side shape check that could
make this unsafe, the
way I was burned on a since-closed sibling PR (#21398) where a kernel
turned out to hardcode a
contract I'd assumed was a bug. The actual GEMM2 kernel this scale feeds
into is closed-source
(`torch_npu`/CANN binary, no Python wrapper to inspect), so I can't rule
that out by reading
source the way I could there.

What I *can* show: for this model specifically, this PR's precondition
(odd scale-group count)
and #21397's precondition (`intermediate_size_per_partition` not a
multiple of 64, i.e. SwiGLU
activation width not 128-aligned) are mathematically the same condition
in disguise —
`intermediate_size_per_partition % 64 == 0` implies
`(intermediate_size_per_partition / 32)` is
even, and conversely an odd scale-group count implies
`intermediate_size_per_partition % 64 != 0`.
So on `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` there is no tensor-parallel size at which
this PR's code path runs
without also hitting #21397 first (SwiGLU quant happens before the
down_proj GEMM this scale
feeds). That means I categorically cannot exercise the padded scale in a
real GEMM2 call on this
model until #21397 is also fixed — not a coincidence of which crash I
hit first, a property of
`moe_intermediate_size=2304` / `group_size=32`. The fix is not
model-specific, though: a
different W4A8-MXFP4 MoE model whose `moe_intermediate_size` doesn't
share this 64/32
relationship could hit the odd-group crash without #21397's constraint,
and would exercise this
code path for real.

So: confirmed correct for the crash it targets (unit test + real
hardware), but end-to-end
correctness of the padded scale inside the actual down_proj GEMM remains
unverified and, for
this specific model, unverifiable until #21397 is resolved too. Flagging
for reviewers rather
than claiming full correctness.

Fixes #21396

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's W4A8-MXFP4 MoE weight loading no longer
crashes when a TP shard
leaves an odd scale-group count. A release-note fragment is included
(release_notes/fragments/21399.yaml).

### How was this patch tested?

- Added
`tests/ut/quantization/methods/w4a8/test_w4a8_mxfp4.py::TestAscendW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod::test_process_weights_pads_odd_tp_scale_groups`,
covering a `(8, 128, 9)` scale shard; confirmed it reproduces the exact
crash
(`RuntimeError: shape '[8, 128, 4, 2]' is invalid for input of size
9216`) against the
unpatched code, and passes with the fix. Also added a round-trip check
that
`restore_weights_for_rl_loading` drops the padding correctly instead of
crashing (caught by
Gemini Code Assist's review — the first version of this fix only handled
the forward
  direction).
- Ran the full `tests/ut/quantization/methods/w4a8/test_w4a8_mxfp4.py`
suite (24 tests) — all pass.
- Verified on real A5 hardware (TP=8, native FP8
`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` checkpoint): this
fix clears the reshape crash and weight loading completes (see caveat

[Feature][SpecDecode] Enable GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash2 graph in PD serving (#22172)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash2 speculative decoding to use FA3 and ACL
Graph in both single-node PD-mixed and two-node PD-disaggregated
serving. This extends the basic DFlash2 support added by #21439.

The change:

- allows supported GLM DFlash2 local drafts to select FA3 without
requiring `enforce_eager=true`;
- keeps common FA3 capability checks active while separating
target-global PP/PCP/DCP and C8 restrictions behind an explicit
local-draft exception;
- preserves the physical `BLHNC/HND/LBHNC` KV-cache layouts while
exposing the zero-copy logical `[page, token, head, dim]` FA3 view;
- safely falls back when the target text config, live loader tag, draft
architecture, dtype, selector capability, hardware, or FA3 operator is
unsupported;
- does not introduce new environment variables, public APIs, or
release-note YAML files.

The branch is rebased onto the latest `main`. The overlap with the
already merged #22159 is resolved by retaining its generic FA3 scheduler
initialization and HND cache fixes, then applying this PR's graph-draft
eligibility and `BLHNC` support on top.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Supported GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash2 deployments can use
`enforce_eager=false` with `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`; target and DFlash2 draft
graphs are captured independently. Unsupported configurations keep their
previous backend selection.

DFlash2 draft capture FULL graphs. Decode consumes the KV cache

[Misc][KV Transfer] Report Mooncake delayed-free status from the sending thread (#22422)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Mooncake's producer control thread can receive a completion notification
and
queue a request for release while the scheduler's drain path is idle
(engine on
0-token steps / the connector gate closed). A small DEBUG-only queue
snapshot
makes pending releases visible during that idle period.

This revision follows the minimal observation design proposed in review
(`wangxiaoteng888/vllm-ascend#6`): a DEBUG-only pending-release sample
instead of
a stalled-drain verdict. The production diff adds 23 lines in
`pull_scheduler.py`:

- Check `logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG)` before invoking the
reporter from
  the existing sending loop.
- At most once per 10 seconds, sample `finished_requests.qsize()` and
log a
nonzero count as `Mooncake delayed-free status: engine_id=...
pending_release=...`.
- Catch observation errors so normal control-message processing can
continue.

The scheduler drain method, DONE handling, heartbeat handling and lease
expiry
logic remain exactly as they were on the baseline. The observer does not
acquire
`state_lock`, track a cross-thread drain flag, scan leases, consume the
queue, or
release blocks. DEBUG disabled skips the reporter entirely; a log-level
check per
control-loop iteration and one initialized timestamp field remain. This
is not a
claim of literally zero overhead or a measured performance improvement.

The release-chain blind spot itself is unchanged: blocks are still
released only
by the drain path (that fix is vllm-ascend#21918). This PR adds
observation only.

### Reading the diagnostic

Enable DEBUG logging on P with the existing launch configuration, run a
small PD
workload, stop new arrivals and keep P/D running. Correlate repeated
`pending_release` samples with P-side `reason=done
action=queued_for_release` and
`Finished sending KV transfer` logs.

The reported queue size is a concurrent snapshot. It does not measure
request age
or count drain operations. The same count in multiple samples can
represent
different requests. A single line, or an unchanged count under ongoing
traffic,
is not proof of a stalled drain. No line means no nonzero queue was
sampled while
logging and the control thread were active; it is not proof of system
health.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

One DEBUG-only diagnostic; no new configuration and no changes to
transfer/release semantics. No release note fragment is included for
this
logging-only change (precedent: vllm-ascend#22643).

### How was this patch tested?

- Four source-isolated CPU repository test cases pass: the DEBUG
disabled/enabled control-loop paths (disabled must not read the clock or
sample
the queue), cadence plus read-only sampling (including an expired lease
left
for the normal drain path, with the bookkeeping snapshot unchanged), and
an
  observation failure that keeps the control loop serving.
- The tests use a logger with its own `logging.Manager`, so a global
`logging.disable()` left behind by another test cannot silence the
sample; this
was confirmed against the local CPU suite where the whole `tests/ut`
tree runs
  in one process.
- `tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_pull_scheduler.py`: 139 passed /
4 failed
  locally, i.e. the same 4 pre-existing pin artifacts as the baseline
(an upstream test calls `get_request_block_hasher` with three arguments
while
  the local vLLM pin still takes two).
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean for both changed files.

NPU inference accuracy, end-to-end performance, and the CI matrix itself
are left
to the pipeline run on this commit.

### Checklist

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: DEBUG-off path, empty queue,
expired
  lease present, and observation error are covered.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: a failing sample is logged and
the
  control loop keeps serving DONE and heartbeat traffic.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: assertions check the actual call
counts of
  the clock and queue sampling, not just log text.
- [x] **Performance impact**: DEBUG-off pays one log-level check per
loop
iteration and no clock read or sampling; DEBUG-on samples once per 10s.

[BugFix] Construct the Qwen4Exp PLE once with prefill context parallelism (#22942)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

During Qwen4Exp initialization with PCP enabled, the decoder builds a
base PLE, allocates its host embedding table and registers it. The
Ascend backbone then deletes the registration and constructs a PCP PLE
for the same layer. This repeats the allocation and registration even on
a single DP replica.

Choose the backend when the upstream decoder constructs each PLE. With
PCP > 1, each worker constructs one Ascend PCP PLE per local PLE layer,
regardless of DP size. With PCP = 1 it constructs one base PLE. The
decoder and the static forward context reference the same instance

the parallel config for each construction. An upstream PLE

[Performance][EPLB] Optimize expert mapping and load recording (#17579)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

In Model Runner V2, EPLB maps each token’s top-k logical expert IDs to
physical experts and records how many tokens each local expert
processed. On main, the map kernel uses a fixed tile of 256 assignments
for both decode and prefill, and the record kernel handles all local
experts in one Triton program.

This PR selects the map tile size from the number of assignments. Small
decode batches can spread work across more cores, while large prefills
process more assignments per tile. The kernel specializes on top-k and
keeps the assignment count dynamic, so batches within a tile size can
reuse a compiled variant. For load recording, each program handles up to
256 local experts, allowing larger expert sets to run across multiple
programs.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The V2 MoE factory registers map warmup for EPLB-enabled routers when
`kernel_config.enable_jit_warmup` is enabled. The existing configuration
and operator interfaces are unchanged. [Release
note](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/108738ac2d243cfb9bc266b3d85d8ebacab7555f/release_notes/fragments/17579.yaml)

decode graph replay and asynchronous EPLB (window 200, interval 300).
Both versions served the full GSM8K test split at concurrency 16 with
the same zero-shot prompts and greedy decoding. Each version ran one
timed pass after warmup.

| GSM8K exact-match accuracy | Main | PR |

#### Operator results against main

The map and record kernels were validated at `b7ac9d60` with CANN 9.2.1

Graph speedup, 16/18 faster |

[BugFix] Skip multimodal lookup on empty MRV2 PCP ranks (#22542)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

A short multimodal prefill can leave an MRV2 PCP rank with zero local
tokens. If that rank's empty query window falls inside an image
placeholder, the vLLM encoder runner asserts before the rank can enter
the padded token embedding collective.

Skip media lookup for an empty PCP rank and return a zero-length mask so
the rank can still participate in the padded embedding exchange. Remove
the wrapper once the paired vLLM includes the guard from
vllm-project/vllm#64435. The corresponding release-branch fix is #22510.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DeepSeek V4.1 multimodal prefill can continue when some PCP ranks
receive zero local tokens for a step.

### How was this patch tested?

- Traced the failing image-window lookup and the padded embedding call
against the vLLM revision pinned by Ascend `main` (`c410543d9`).
- Added regression coverage for an empty PCP rank inside an image span
and a non-PCP delegation control in
`test_pcp_multimodal_embedding_padding.py`.

#### Four-rank PCP regression

Ran the same two-token MRV2 image-prefill case on Ascend A3 with CANN
9.3.0 and vLLM `c410543d9`. Both revisions partitioned the two tokens as
`[1, 1, 0, 0]`.

- On `main` (`338540511`), ranks 2 and 3 hit `assert start_idx <
end_idx` in `encoder_runner.py:260`. Ranks 0 and 1 entered HCCL
all-gather and remained there until the test terminated the group.
- At the PR head (`4ff1923fc`), all four ranks completed real HCCL
all-gather and reduce-scatter. Token embeddings, merged image
embeddings, and the empty-rank padding buffers matched expectations.

#### MMMU accuracy

Ran the first 100 MMMU validation samples in dataset order, three times
at concurrency 64, on the same A3 system and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
`1017-w4a8` checkpoint as #22510. The standalone MRV2 service used
TP1/PCP8/DP2, DSpark with 5 draft tokens, and CANN 9.3.0. Request hashes
matched the release runs for every sample.

The PR head hit an Engram post-load error at startup. The scored run
used local test commit `af2c52c18`, which adds the runtime fixes from
#22521 and #22530 to `4ff1923fc`. The launcher used `TMPDIR=/tmp` for
the CANN Unix sockets.

[Feature] Support layerwise KV cache reuse in Mooncake connector (#21891)

### What does this PR do?

Mooncake Push can submit a WRITE after the model has advanced to another
layer. When AscendStore offload rotates layers through shared NPU KV
slots, Push must submit each shared-layer WRITE while its source pages
are valid and signal completion before the store can overwrite them.

- Give the Push scheduler the producer block tables even when
AscendStore supplies the prefix hit.
- Submit shared-layer reads from the layer hook, fence their WRITE
futures before reuse, and leave resident caches on the existing deferred
path.
- Pass the KDA layer name through the save hook so its final prompt
state can be sent before slot reuse.

Depends on #21256 for the model-aware shared layout. This PR targets
main so the review contains only the Push adaptation. The shared-slot
path requires the two PRs together.

### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

Together with #21256, it enables `MooncakePushConnector` in a producer
`MultiConnector` with AscendStore layerwise prefill offload. The
existing configuration controls offload.

[Performance][Model] Fuse rotated Engram gate on Ascend A3 (#21442)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Rotated DeepSeek V4.1 checkpoints on A3 currently expand Engram RMS
normalization, weighted correlation, gate/mask and residual injection
into many kernels. This adds an A3-specific Triton kernel for those
operations while retaining the separate FP32 block32 inverse-rotation
MatMul.

Hardware paths remain explicit:

| Hardware/checkpoint | Path |
| --- | --- |
| A3, rotated | Separate inverse-rotation MatMul + new chunked A3 fused
gate |
| A5, unrotated | Existing A5 fused gate, unchanged |
| Other combinations | Existing unfused implementation |

Only A3 receives `ENGRAM_ROTATED_GATE`. The original A5 kernel file is
byte-for-byte identical to main. The slower all-in-one rotation
experiments are excluded.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: faster rotated DeepSeek V4.1 Engram execution on A3. No new flags,
environment variables, dependencies or API changes. `wkv`, lookup/hash
preparation and the checkpoint's rotation semantics are preserved.

### How was this patch tested?

**A3 hardware:** Ascend910_9362, torch 2.10.0+cpu, torch_npu
2.10.0.post4.dev20260715, Triton-Ascend 3.2.0. Candidate main modules
were loaded in an isolated namespace over the existing container without
replacing its installation.


`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_engram_gate.py`:
**16 passed** on A3. Coverage includes BF16/FP16, 96/5120 channels,
1/132/432 token rows, non-contiguous row strides, masked-token identity,
wrong-basis regression, updated-input ACL graph replay, and six
real-profile dispatch combinations across A2/A3/A5 and rotated/unrotated
inputs. The A5-profile dispatch check executes on A3; it is not an A5
hardware-validation claim.

Reproduce in a main-compatible NPU environment:

```bash
ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 pytest -q -s \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_engram_gate.py
```

**Matched microbenchmark:** `[132, 4, 5120]`, BF16, ACL graph replay,
five samples of 30 replays after warmup:

| Post-wkv path, including inverse rotation | Median |
| --- | ---: |
| Unfused | 262.153 us |
| A3 fused gate | 79.423 us |

This is approximately 3.30x faster for this stage. It excludes `wkv`
GEMM and table lookup; no full-model TPOT gain is claimed. The test
asserts that the fused stage outperforms the unfused stage. Working
memory is bounded by the current tensors and a 1024-channel reduction
tile; no history, subprocess or host synchronization is added to the
production path.

**Checks:** Ruff check/format, codespell, typos, clang-format,
markdownlint, Python-package init, forbidden-import,
boolean-context-manager, long-function, symbolic-meta and logger checks
passed. Changed Python files pass syntax/LF checks and `git diff
--check`.

**Local environment limitations:** `bash format.sh ci` was attempted.
The full aggregate command is not claimed to pass: Actionlint's
environment installation did not finish; a subsequent run skipped that
hook. Gitleaks/logger shebang execution and ShellCheck were unavailable
on Windows, and system hooks invoking the Windows `python3` alias
failed. Logger, long-function and symbolic-meta checks were rerun
explicitly with available interpreters and passed. Repository-wide LF
auditing also finds 50 pre-existing CRLF files and missing global LF
configuration; this PR does not change those unrelated files. A5
hardware and full-model acceptance remain unrun.

### CI rebase compatibility fix (2026-11-18)

The E2E workflow's `pre-commit` job passed on `f31f8b67b`, but both
CPU-UT matrix jobs failed before running tests: `_selected_tests.yaml`
rebases the PR onto main, which discarded the merge resolution and
replayed the original conflicting commit. Replaced the merge-based
history with one signed-off linear commit, `7eae80dd7`, rebased onto
main `9f45ef9bc`. The squashed tree was verified identical to the

explicit SHA lease.

Local rebase onto current main succeeds; affected-file Ruff
check/format, syntax/LF and `git diff --check` pass. CPU/NPU runtime
tests remain pending on the new head. Requested a fresh E2E run via
`/run`. The earlier resolution and hardware evidence below are
historical, not a CI-pass claim for this new commit.

Validation for this update: affected-file Ruff check/format, codespell,

[Feature] Integrate Ascend sleep mode backend (#22822)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Align vLLM Ascend sleep mode with the upstream pluggable sleep-backend
interface
([vllm-project/vllm#44074](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44074)).

Today `NPUWorker.sleep/wake_up` talks to `CaMemAllocator` directly.
Upstream
now dispatches sleep through `SleepModeBackend` and
`SleepModeBackendFactory`, so Ascend keeps a private copy of the
dispatch
logic and cannot benefit from upstream backend selection or future
backends.

This PR adds the minimal
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/22572 P1 integration:

- Add `CaMemBackend(SleepModeBackend)` in
  `vllm_ascend/device_allocator/sleep_mode_backend.py`, backed by
`CaMemAllocator`. It implements `suspend`, `resume`, and `discard`, and
  keeps the upstream `SleepModeBackend` state machine.
- Register the backend as `"camem"` at import time using the upstream
`SleepModeBackendFactory`, matching how upstream registers its built-in
  `"cumem"` backend.
- Normalize the default `"cumem"` name to `"camem"` in
`NPUPlatform.check_and_update_config()` when sleep mode is enabled. This
  avoids modifying the private `SleepModeBackendFactory._registry` while
  keeping `--enable-sleep-mode` usable without an explicit backend flag.
- Inherit the upstream `sleep_mode_backend` property in `NPUWorker` and
dispatch sleep/wake through `self.sleep_mode_backend.suspend(level)` and
  `.resume(tags)`.
- Keep the existing level-2 snapshot, `global_te` unregister/reregister,
NZ
  check, and RL extra-cleanup behavior unchanged.

This PR is intentionally P1 only. Moving level-2 to allocation-level
`discardable` handling is a separate follow-up.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Mostly no; there is one visible config normalization:

- `--enable-sleep-mode` still works without `--sleep-mode-backend`.
- The default backend name is normalized from `"cumem"` to `"camem"` on
  Ascend when sleep mode is enabled, so config dumps/logs may show
  `"camem"`.
- An explicit `--sleep-mode-backend cumem` is also normalized to
`"camem"`.
- `--sleep-mode-backend camem` can be selected explicitly.
- Third-party backends are not affected on both v0.33 and pinned main, a
third-party backend is rejected during config before sleep changes
worker state.

### Compatibility

- **vLLM 0.33:** `NPUWorker.sleep` passes `level`;
`CaMemBackend.suspend`
  implements the level-based contract. 
- **Pinned main:** the in-tree `camem` backend continues to accept the
level
  passed by `NPUWorker`. 
- Third-party backends are rejected before
`global_te.unregister_buffer()`.
The guard raises a clear `ValueError` before any worker state is
changed.
- **torch_npu 2.10:** no new torch_npu APIs are required.

[BugFix] Reassemble SSE frames in the PD load balance proxies (#22787)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #22478.

The PD disaggregation load balance proxies parsed each network chunk of
the
decode backend's response on its own:

```python
chunk_str = chunk.decode("utf-8").strip()
if chunk_str.startswith("data: "):
    chunk_str = chunk_str[len("data: ") :]
chunk_json = json.loads(chunk_str)   # <- per chunk, not per frame
```

The decode backend answers with SSE (`data: {json}` frames terminated by
`data: [DONE]`), but the network does not respect frame boundaries:

* **A frame split across two reads.** Its JSON is cut in the middle, so
  `json.loads()` fails on both halves and the frame is dropped.
* **Two frames coalesced into one read.** `json.loads()` requires the
whole
input to be a single JSON value, so the trailing `data: [DONE]` sentinel
  poisons the parse and a complete response is dropped.

In both cases the proxy loses the frame, and with it the `stop_reason`
it
needs to drive its recompute retry. A request that the decode backend
aborted
with `stop_reason="recomputed"` is therefore never retried, and the
aborted
generation reaches the client instead of a re-routed one. The token
accounting used for the retry's `max_tokens` budget is wrong for the
same
reason.

This change makes both proxies reassemble the byte stream into SSE
frames
before decoding them:

* New shared helper
`examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/sse_frame_parser.py`.
  `SSEFrameParser` buffers incoming bytes, splits them on the SSE frame
terminator, and decodes each frame with
`json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode()`,
which consumes only the first complete JSON value and leaves any
trailing
  bytes for the next frame.
* The streaming loop iterates over the frames a chunk completed instead
of
assuming one chunk carries one frame. A chunk that completes no frame is
  forwarded verbatim and the rest of the frame is awaited.
* The original bytes are still forwarded to the client unchanged unless
the
  proxy has to rewrite the payload (cached-token injection, or the
  non-streaming reply), so the wire format is unchanged.

The frame buffer is reset at every decoder attempt boundary, because
each
attempt emits a self-contained stream.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes — a bug fix. The PD disaggregation load balance proxy no longer
drops
decoder responses whose SSE frame did not align with a network read, so
the
recompute retry now triggers reliably instead of leaking the aborted
generation to the client. A release note fragment is included
(`release_notes/fragments/22787.yaml`).

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests only (no NPU hardware needed — the change is in the proxy
examples, which run on CPU).

```
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 pytest -sv tests/ut/proxy
57 passed
```

New tests:

* `tests/ut/proxy/test_sse_frame_parser.py` — unit tests for the parser:
complete frame, frame split across chunks, two frames coalesced into one
chunk, byte-at-a-time delivery, the `[DONE]` sentinel, non-SSE frames, a
  trailing frame without a terminator, a malformed frame, and a split at
  every offset of a frame.
* `tests/ut/proxy/test_load_balance_proxy_server.py` — end-to-end HTTP
tests
against the mock decode backend: a frame split across two network
chunks, a
frame coalesced with `[DONE]`, a frame delivered one byte per chunk, and
  the recompute retry firing for a split frame and for a coalesced read.
* `tests/ut/proxy/test_load_balance_proxy_layerwise_server.py` — the
same
  reassembly and recompute-retry behaviour for the layerwise proxy.

Each regression test was checked to fail before the fix and pass after
it:

```

FAILED test_stream_frames_coalesced_in_one_chunk
FAILED test_stream_byte_at_a_time
FAILED test_recompute_detected_when_frame_split_across_chunks
```

[BugFix][KV Pool] Size layerwise objects by group payload extent (#20856)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Memcache layerwise pooling extrapolates each cache group's per-layer
bytes to the full model layer count. Model like GLM 5.3 flash, the
hybrid groups with only 11–12 layers can therefore reserve capacity for
45–46 layers. PP stages also retain a global-layer-derived byte origin
inside their own stage-qualified objects, leaving an unused prefix.

This PR sizes each object from its **registered group payload**：

- Size each shard from `sum(group_block_len[group_id])`, including
registered MTP entries, rather than the full-model layer estimate.
- Remove the PP byte origin from both allocation and
`LayerBatchBuilder`. PP stages already use distinct `@pp{rank}` keys, so
each stage's payload can start at byte zero within its shard.

- Remove the redundant shared-KV allocation override introduced by
#21949. `LayerwiseKVPoolWorker` now inherits
`BaseKVPoolWorker._global_group_alloc_size`, so object allocation and
builders share the same group-payload sizing and DCP alignment. This
does not add DS4.1 PP/DCP support.

#### GLM-5.3-Flash layouts: PP2/PCP8

The target model has 45 layers: 34 KDA layers and 11 sparse MLA layers.
The standard grouping used by this example is:

| Group | Cached data | Target physical layers | Normal KVPool prefix
transfer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| G0 | Main MLA cache + completed compressed-indexer cache; both share
scheduler block IDs | 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 27, 31, 35, 39, 43 | Yes |
| G1 | Request-private compressor-tail ring | Same MLA layers as G0 |
No: `prefix_cacheable=False` |
| G2 | KDA convolution + recurrent state | 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28,
32, 36, 40, 44 | At eligible checkpoint boundaries, subject to masks |
| G3 | KDA convolution + recurrent state | 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29,
33, 37, 41 | At eligible checkpoint boundaries, subject to masks |
| G4 | KDA convolution + recurrent state | 2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22, 26, 30,
34, 38, 42 | At eligible checkpoint boundaries, subject to masks |

When ordinary MTP L45 is registered in this same plan, it adds one
physical layer to G0 and its corresponding tail to G1. For the `23,22`
target partition used below, the resulting **unique physical-layer
counts** are:

| Group | PP2 stage 0: L0–L22 | PP2 stage 1: L23–L44 + MTP L45 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| G0 | 5 | 7 |
| G1 (local tail only) | 5 | 7 |
| G2 | 6 | 6 |
| G3 | 6 | 5 |
| G4 | 6 | 5 |

A physical MLA layer therefore has cache components in both G0 and G1,
but only G0 participates in the normal KVPool object layouts below.
Multiple MLA/indexer entries within G0 still count as one physical
layer. KDA objects contain state snapshots at valid boundaries rather
than per-token K/V. Group IDs assume this standard target + ordinary-MTP
plan; separate draft groups must be checked against the actual
`KVCacheConfig`.

**Current layerwise key composition and object contents**

The following describes normal complete-prefix objects for **TP1 / PP2 /
PCP8 / DCP1**, with ordinary MTP registered as above and KVPP off.

```text
MLA (G0), stage s:
  {model}@0@pp{s}@{block_hash_hex}@0

KDA (g = G2/G3/G4), stage s, PCP head shard r:
  {model}@{group_id}@pp{s}@{block_hash_hex}@0@pcp_size:8@pcp_rank:{r}
```

Here `s=0..1`, `group_id=2,3,4`, and `r=0..7`. The rank field before the
PCP suffix is `0` because TP=1. A complete key identifies **one group
object for one logical block/state boundary, PP stage, and relevant
rank/shard**. It contains every registered physical layer of that group
on the stage.

Read from left to right in increasing offset from that key's base GVA.
For the current DCP1 layout, layers are packed in group-local
physical-layer order:

```text
key -> object [V, V + payload); address increases left to right ->
┌───────────────────────┬────────────────────────┬─────┬──────────────────────┐
│ first layer's entries │ second layer's entries │ ... │ last layer's entries │
└───────────────────────┴────────────────────────┴─────┴──────────────────────┘

GVA(entry e) = V + sum(group_block_len[group_id][:e])
copy length  = group_block_len[group_id][e]
```

<details>
<summary>Expand the current keys and the layer chunks stored under each
key</summary>

A bar cell labeled `Lx` denotes **all registered entries for that
physical layer within the selected group**, concatenated by their actual
lengths. Each complete bar represents one key's object. A KDA layer
chunk is a boundary-state snapshot for the selected head shard.

**PP2 / PCP8 / DCP1 / TP1, target partition `23,22`**

The two MLA objects are shared identities across PCP replicas. Each KDA
line below expands to eight distinct keys, with `r=0..7`; its contents
belong only to PCP head shard `r`.

```text
Stage 0:

GLM-5.3-Flash@0@pp0@H@0
  ┌────┬────┬─────┬─────┬─────┐
  │ L3 │ L7 │ L11 │ L15 │ L19 │  MLA/indexer
  └────┴────┴─────┴─────┴─────┘

GLM-5.3-Flash@2@pp0@H@0@pcp_size:8@pcp_rank:r
  ┌────┬────┬────┬─────┬─────┬─────┐
  │ L0 │ L4 │ L8 │ L12 │ L16 │ L20 │  KDA shard r
  └────┴────┴────┴─────┴─────┴─────┘

GLM-5.3-Flash@3@pp0@H@0@pcp_size:8@pcp_rank:r
  ┌────┬────┬────┬─────┬─────┬─────┐
  │ L1 │ L5 │ L9 │ L13 │ L17 │ L21 │  KDA shard r
  └────┴────┴────┴─────┴─────┴─────┘

GLM-5.3-Flash@4@pp0@H@0@pcp_size:8@pcp_rank:r
  ┌────┬────┬─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┐
  │ L2 │ L6 │ L10 │ L14 │ L18 │ L22 │  KDA shard r
  └────┴────┴─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┘

Stage 1:

GLM-5.3-Flash@0@pp1@H@0
  ┌─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┐
  │ L23 │ L27 │ L31 │ L35 │ L39 │ L43 │ L45 │  MLA/indexer
  └─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┘

GLM-5.3-Flash@2@pp1@H@0@pcp_size:8@pcp_rank:r
  ┌─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┐
  │ L24 │ L28 │ L32 │ L36 │ L40 │ L44 │  KDA shard r
  └─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┘

GLM-5.3-Flash@3@pp1@H@0@pcp_size:8@pcp_rank:r
  ┌─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┐
  │ L25 │ L29 │ L33 │ L37 │ L41 │  KDA shard r
  └─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┘

GLM-5.3-Flash@4@pp1@H@0@pcp_size:8@pcp_rank:r
  ┌─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┐
  │ L26 │ L30 │ L34 │ L38 │ L42 │  KDA shard r
  └─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┘
```

</details>

#### Before and Later

Compare three sizing approaches: **Full-model estimate** (`3e9e1869a`,
PP byte offset retained), **Group payload with PP offset**
(`8c5b148b1`), and **Group payload without PP offset** (`5b46746f8`).
Here, “PP offset” means the extra byte offset inside the pool object.

The example uses **PP=2, PCP=8, TP=1, DCP=1** with target partition
`23,22`: stage 0 owns L0–L22; stage 1 owns L23–L44 plus ordinary MTP
L45.

It uses Memcache layerwise transfer, KVPP off, RecoverSSM off, and
ordinary MTP L45 registered in the same cache plan. MTP3 means three
speculative tokens, not three extra physical layers.

For readable arithmetic, use **synthetic registered payloads**: 1 MiB
per G0 MLA/indexer layer and 128 KiB per KDA layer's PCP head shard.
Real sizes come from `group_block_len` and depend on the actual
model/cache metadata. The old full-model estimate uses 45 layers in this
PP2 configuration.

**G0 allocation per key:**

| PP stage | G0 layers / payload | Full-model estimate | Group payload
with PP offset | Group payload without PP offset |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 5 / 5 MiB | 45 MiB | 5 MiB | 5 MiB |
| 1 | 7 / 7 MiB | 45 MiB | 30 MiB | 7 MiB |

This configuration has **DCP=1**, so it applies no DCP shard stride or
associated 2 MiB alignment. PCP8 does not create eight regions inside
one MLA key. These are synthetic layout calculations, not physical DRAM
measurements.

<details>
<summary>Expand GLM MLA keys, before/after space maps, and
addressing</summary>

Each version is drawn as **one horizontal object bar**, with offsets
increasing left to right; cell widths are not to scale. All intervals
are half-open ranges relative to **each key's base GVA**. All ranges
below use MiB. `H` is a symbolic hash for an eligible block/state
boundary in the relevant group and configuration; matching placeholders
do not assert cross-topology cache compatibility.

**MLA: PP stages own separate compact objects**

For MLA, the PCP gather makes the cache contents replicated across PCP
workers. With DCP=1, the pool save-owner check selects PCP0 (and TP0
here). The other seven PCP workers do not append seven extra payload
regions to that MLA object.

```text
key: GLM-5.3-Flash@0@pp0@H@0
payload: stage 0's L3,7,11,15,19
unit: MiB; address increases ->

Full-model estimate: 45 MiB
┌───────────────────┬───────────────────────────┐
│ PP0 payload [0,5) │ unused reservation [5,45) │
└───────────────────┴───────────────────────────┘

Group payload with / without PP offset: 5 MiB
┌───────────────────┐
│ PP0 payload [0,5) │
└───────────────────┘

key: GLM-5.3-Flash@0@pp1@H@0
payload: stage 1's L23,27,31,35,39,43,45
unit: MiB; address increases ->

Full-model estimate: 45 MiB
┌────────────────┬─────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┐
│ PP hole [0,23) │ PP1 payload [23,30) │ unused reservation [30,45) │
└────────────────┴─────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┘

Group payload with PP offset: 30 MiB
┌────────────────┬─────────────────────┐
│ PP hole [0,23) │ PP1 payload [23,30) │
└────────────────┴─────────────────────┘

Group payload without PP offset: 7 MiB
┌───────────────────┐
│ PP1 payload [0,7) │
└───────────────────┘
```

The stage 0 object never fills the stage 1 object's prefix hole: `@pp0`
and `@pp1` identify separate keys. The layout without a PP byte offset
removes that hole while preserving PP key tags and layer numbering.

For stage 1's **L31**, global 31 → stage-local 8 → G0 ordinal 2. Its
start relative to `GLM-5.3-Flash@0@pp1@H@0` is:

| Sizing approach | G0 object capacity | L31 start |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full-model estimate | 45 MiB | 23 + 2 = 25 MiB |
| Group payload with PP offset | 30 MiB | 23 + 2 = 25 MiB |
| Group payload without PP offset | 7 MiB | 0 + 2 = 2 MiB |

These offsets are the same for PCP readers of that MLA key. There is no
`pcp_rank * shard_stride` term. The local HBM address still uses each
reader's own entry base and request block ID.

For an eligible boundary that newly saves both MLA stage objects, the
allocation totals are:

| Distinct MLA keys | Full-model estimate | Group payload with PP offset
| Group payload without PP offset |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2 (one per PP stage) | 90 MiB | 35 MiB | 12 MiB |

The totals are the two G0 object allocations added together: `45 + 45`,
`5 + 30`, and `5 + 7` MiB respectively. They use the teaching payload
sizes above and exclude backend overhead.

The retained MLA example is covered by **48 worker/group layouts** from
the CPU source-extracted checks across all three revisions (2 PP stages
× 8 PCP ranks × 3 revisions). These checks cover save ownership,
allocation, and layer-copy bounds. Current-head NPU/Memcache
save/restore and model validation remain pending below.

</details>

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Memcache layerwise objects reserve capacity for the registered
group payload without PP padding.

**Cache-layout migration is required.** PP payload origins change even
when DCP is disabled, and shared-DCP strides can shrink. Upgrade all
writers and readers together, and rebuild affected persisted
PP/shared-DCP objects or use a fresh cache namespace. Restarting workers
alone does not invalidate old objects. Participants sharing keys must
use matching PP partitions, DCP topology, and group layouts.

### How was this patch tested?

**Rebase validation (2026-11-20):**

- Rebased onto Ascend main `b9e7ab251`; `git range-diff` confirms all
four replayed patches are unchanged.
- **350 CPU tests passed** with the branch's verified vLLM source
`c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15`. Test startup passed the

of this rebased head: **CI testing only**. The hardware results below

With the Ascend checkout and the verified vLLM source on `PYTHONPATH`,

[Refactor][V2] Move kernel block handling into AttentionGroup (#20758)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Following [vLLM PR
#57169](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57169), move kernel
block size selection and mapping into `AttentionGroup` in Ascend V2.
Attention groups within the same KV cache group can use different kernel
block sizes.

- Keep block tables and slot mappings at manager-block granularity. Use
each attention group’s kernel block size for attention metadata and KV
cache views.
- Adapt PCP global block tables and block counts, and update DFlash and
DSpark to consume manager block tables.
- Preserve kernel-granular tables on 310P until its runner provides
manager-granular tables.

#### Triton operator changes

Attention groups sharing a KV cache group may need different kernel
block sizes. The shared table therefore keeps manager block IDs, and
each `AttentionGroup` expands them into its own kernel blocks; both
operators below now use manager blocks for lookup and slot arithmetic.

- **`compute_slot_mappings`** takes request-row indices, token
positions, and manager block tables, and writes flat KV-cache slot IDs
through the shared V2 entry point
`AscendBlockTables.compute_slot_mappings`. With table expansion moved to
`AttentionGroup`, it now uses the manager block size for lookup and slot
arithmetic. DCP-sharded groups first convert positions to rank-local
positions.
- **`prepare_dflash_inputs_triton`** takes target-batch metadata,
sampling state, and manager block tables, and fills preallocated
draft-token, position, KV-slot, and sampling buffers for DFlash and
DSpark. Both callers now pass manager block tables. The launcher uses
one runtime `block_size` for DCP and lookup, and `block_stride` for
physical block spacing.

#### Triton JIT specialization

Slot mapping reads manager block sizes from a tensor; DFlash uses
runtime `block_size` and `block_stride` for manager-block address
arithmetic. The remaining compile-time parameters follow the existing
implementation. Changes to those constants, argument dtypes, or Triton's
default runtime specialization classes can still require a new compiled
version; these are existing specialization rules, not new triggers
introduced by this PR. In the measured workload below, main and PR
produced the same numbers of cache variants and actual compilations.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No user-facing changes.

### How was this patch tested?

This refactor retains the operators' existing device support; the
standalone operator validation reported here was performed on Ascend A3.

The end-to-end accuracy and performance runs used W8A8 models on Ascend
A3 with [vLLM
`c410543d9`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15),
expert parallelism, and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`.

- **DeepSeek V4-Flash-0731** used DP4 × PCP4, TP1, and 7-step DSpark.
- **GLM-5.3-Flash** used TP8 × PCP2 and 5-step MTP.

A focused CPU regression run with vLLM `c410543d9` passed 7 kernel-table
capacity cases, including expansion of 6 manager columns into 12 kernel
IDs for encoder–decoder capacity and reuse of sufficiently sized
buffers.

#### Single-operator correctness

On one Ascend A3 die, slot mapping passed **11 cases** and DFlash input
preparation passed **28 cases** against independent host references. All
compared outputs matched elementwise, with a maximum absolute error of
**0** and **0** mismatched elements. The rerun used CANN 9.2.0, Python
3.12.13, PyTorch 2.10.0, torch-npu 2.10.0.post7, Triton-Ascend 3.6.0,
and vLLM `c410543d9`. It used the vLLM-Ascend `98d8a92c` build with the
updated tests and byte-identical operator and launcher code.

- Slot mapping replays the captured 79-token DeepSeek V4 Flash prefill
shape and checks that a disabled KV group is filled with `PAD_ID`.
- DFlash checks that `num_reqs_override` processes only the selected
requests, writes graph padding, and leaves skipped request data intact.

```bash
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_compute_slot_mapping.py \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_prepare_dflash_inputs.py
```

#### JIT compilation

DeepSeek V4-Flash-0731 W8A8 ran on 8 A3 dies (DP2 × PCP4, TP1, 7-step
DSpark). Main `de6351f5` and PR `98d8a92c` each started with an empty
Triton cache and ran three prompts (79, 555, and 2,731 tokens),
generating 32 tokens per request, then repeated them. Both revisions had
the same counts (slot mapping / draft inputs).

|---|---:|---:|
| Startup | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| First request pass | 1 / 3 | 4 / 12 |
| Repeat pass | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

A separate run with a Triton compiler listener counted compilations
across workers, excluding cache hits. The slot-mapping tile and gather
window were both 1024. Draft input context tiles were 2, 16, and 64. No
additional variants or compilations were observed for the PR in this
workload. This change adds no JIT warmup registrations, so
registration-specific tests do not apply.

#### Accuracy

We evaluated all 1,319 GSM8K test questions with BS128, a 256K context
limit, up to 128K output tokens, and temperature 0. Generation stopped
at EOS or the output limit. Accuracy is shown as main / PR.

- **DeepSeek**: 96.74% / 96.51%.
- **GLM**: 97.27% / 97.50%.

#### Single-operator performance

We compared main `de6351f5` and PR `98d8a92c` on one Ascend A3 die with

[Performance] Keep quantized PLE scales in HBM for host-offloaded embeddings (#22734)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The Qwen4Exp PLE lookup reads one scale per group of 32 embedding codes.
Fetching those scales over host UVA is expensive when many tokens select
the same small set of rows. Keep each rank's local scale shard in HBM
and continue fetching the codes from the registered host table. With DP
shared memory, only the owner writes the shared codes and every replica
loads its own scales. The Triton lookup also accepts the existing
chunk-pointer scale representation.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Quantized host offload uses an additional 1 byte of HBM per 32 local
embedding elements for MXFP8 and 4 bytes per 32 for INT8, per replica.
The checkpoint layout and invocation stay the same.

### How was this patch tested?

| Dataset | Hardware | Accuracy |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| GPQA | Ascend 950DT | 91.92% |

- 58 tests passed in the Ascend service environment across the quantized
PLE and host-offload unit suites, including DP ownership and
partial-allocation cleanup.

On Ascend 950DT, the placement microbenchmark kept MXFP8 embedding codes
in host memory and varied scale placement. Embedding width was 160 and
the ID tensor shape was `[8192, 16]`. Each cell reports median lookup
latency over nine device-event measurements.

| Access pattern | Host scales (baseline) | HBM scales | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 hot owned rows | 12.52 ms | 2.92 ms | 4.28× |
| Uniformly sampled owned rows | 2.44 ms | 2.27 ms | 1.07× |

The microbenchmark addresses both placements through pointer tables. The
production path passes the dense HBM scale tensor directly.

**16K prefill serving benchmark (AISBench)**

Both runs used the same GSM8K-derived request file, with 16,384 input
tokens and one output token per request. The prefill side used four
Ascend 950DT devices (TP2 × DP2), an 8,192-token batch budget, and
prefix caching disabled. The configured request rate was 1.9 requests/s
with a concurrency cap of 64. All 256 requests succeeded in each run.

| Scale placement | Mean TTFT | P90 TTFT | P99 TTFT | Completed
requests/s | Input tokens/s per prefill device |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Host (baseline) | 2,614.7 ms | 4,499.8 ms | 7,256.9 ms | 1.8814 |
7,706.37 |
| HBM | 2,441.3 ms | 3,743.3 ms | 5,131.3 ms | 1.8766 | 7,686.64 |

Mean TTFT was 6.6% lower in this pair of runs. Input throughput differed
by 0.3% at the configured request rate. Each placement was measured

[Feature][kv_transfer] Support do_virtual in MooncakeConnectorV2 (#22557)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add per-request `do_virtual` support to the default pull path of
`MooncakeConnectorV2`, following the existing V1 behavior.

This supports D-side inference without requiring a live P service or
receiving KV cache from P.

For virtual requests:
- Propagate `do_virtual` through connector metadata.
- Report receive completion locally instead of submitting remote KV
reads.
- Skip producer lease validation, heartbeats, and completion
notifications.
- Handle zero-external-token and cancellation paths without contacting
P.

The flag defaults to false, preserving normal PD behavior.
Layerwise push is outside the scope of this change.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Requests to a D service using the default MooncakeConnectorV2 pull
path
can set `do_virtual: true` in `kv_transfer_params`, together with
`do_remote_prefill: true` and the existing required remote metadata.

D then completes the receive phase locally and continues inference
without P.
Generated text is only used to check request completion; it is not an
accuracy result because the historical KV cache was not transferred.

### How was this patch tested?

1. V1 reference behavior:
- Started a Qwen3-8B D service with MooncakeConnectorV1, TP1, without P.
- Sent three virtual requests with 256 prompt tokens and `max_tokens=2`.

- Confirmed real KV transfer in worker logs and producer release after

3. V2 virtual health probe:

completion.

[Revert] Revert "[BugFix][MoE] Share DSpark MegaMoE contexts across CANN buffer APIs" (#21727) (#22964)

Revert of PR #21727 (merged onto `main`).

Original PR: #21727
Original author: @rikakuhi
Merge commit: `96ce11dc669b167d04402e94fc0fada32499a6b4`

---
### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4.1 with DSpark and CANN MegaMoE creates separate target and
draft buffers on the same MC2 group. On A5, the second native context
can contain zero peer-buffer addresses, causing MegaMoE to fail during
startup profiling.

Keep one target-owned allocation on the MC2 group coordinator and give
the draft an independent metadata view over the same context and context
manager. Validate communication settings and capacity before sharing.
Identify MRv2 eager drafts by logical expert counts, including redundant
experts.

Bind CANN capacity queries by parameter name to support both the legacy
interface and the current interface with `intermediate_hidden`,
`combine_comm_mode`, and topology-dependent `server_num`. This updates
the approach in #20234 for current main and CANN 9.2.1 while preserving
main's buffer-sizing policy. Target and draft calls remain serialized.

During wake-up, the first stale model view rebinds the group-owned CANN
context and runs a barrier. Target and draft both refresh their own
runtime metadata from that context. The packaged MLA stream-lifetime
change is tracked in #22592.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Fixes conflicting MegaMoE communication contexts for DeepSeek V4.1
DSpark on A5. No additional configuration is required. Includes a
release note fragment.

### How was this patch tested?

- Focused CPU regression and lifecycle tests: **17 passed** with Python
3.12, torch 2.10.0, and vLLM `24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58`:

  ```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty python3 -m
pytest -q \
    --confcutdir=tests/ut/ops \
    tests/ut/ops/test_mega_moe_context.py \
    tests/ut/ops/test_fused_mc2_sleep_state.py
  ```

- The deployment backport passed **26 CPU tests**, including
`test_moe_comm_method.py`.
- A smoke check against the installed CANN 9.2.1 native capacity-query
API passed for target 384 experts/top-k 6 and draft 128 experts/top-k 3
with P and D capacity settings. Each pair used one mocked allocation and
shared context identity.
- Ruff lint/format, codespell, typos, Python package initialization,
forbidden-import, and boolean-context checks passed.

- Review follow-up: **30 CPU unit tests passed** on Linux AArch64 with
Python 3.12.13, PyTorch `2.10.0+cpu`, pytest 8.4.2 and vLLM
`24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58`. Ran `python3 -m pytest -q
-ra` on `test_mega_moe_context.py`, `test_moe_comm_method.py` and
`test_fused_mc2_sleep_state.py` with the repository CPU mocks. The new
sleep/wake-up case covers both target-first and draft-first recovery. A5
hardware coverage remains pending.
